holidays.name: National Dentist's Day
holidays.description: A day to thank the folks who stare into your mouth, judge your flossing habits, and still manage to smile. Celebrate by actually flossing, or at least by promising your dentist that you will.
holidays.origin: Observed in the United States on March 6 and popularized through the 1990s and 2000s by dental associations and unofficial holiday calendars. It exists to recognize dentists for their work in oral health and to encourage regular checkups.
holidays.funFact: Before modern dentistry, tooth pain was sometimes treated by barbers, who pulled teeth alongside giving haircuts and shaves. The red and white barber pole is said to hint at their bloody side jobs.

holidays.name: National Oreo Cookie Day
holidays.description: A day to twist, lick, dunk, and devour the world's most famous sandwich cookie. Debate the proper way to eat one with friends and family, and expect strong opinions.
holidays.origin: Oreo cookies were first introduced by Nabisco in 1912, and March 6 has become a popular unofficial day to celebrate them in the United States. Social media and food marketers helped the day take off.
holidays.funFact: Oreos are often said to be the best-selling cookie in the United States, and the classic design has a pattern of 12 petals on each cookie wafer. Some claim that more than 450 billion have been sold worldwide.

holidays.name: National Frozen Food Day
holidays.description: A salute to the freezer aisle, where peas, pizzas, and last night's questionable leftovers wait patiently for their moment. Celebrate by cooking an all-frozen dinner and feeling no shame.
holidays.origin: The day was proclaimed by President Ronald Reagan in 1984 to honor the frozen food industry, and it is observed on March 6. It recognizes how freezing changed food storage and convenience.
holidays.funFact: Modern frozen food owes a lot to Clarence Birdseye, who got the idea for flash freezing after seeing Inuit people in Labrador freeze fish almost instantly in frigid air.

holidays.name: National Dance Day (Marathon Dance Day)
holidays.description: A day to show off your best moves, whether it's a waltz, a wiggle, or flailing around the kitchen while the pasta boils. No talent required, only enthusiasm and maybe a stretch first.
holidays.origin: Several unofficial calendars list dance-related celebrations in early March as a way to promote fitness and joy through movement. The day is loosely tied to the dance marathon fad that swept America in the 1920s and 1930s.
holidays.funFact: During the Great Depression, dance marathons could last for weeks, with contestants competing for cash prizes while shuffling around nearly nonstop. The record is said to be over 3,000 hours.

holidays.name: World Day of Muscle Relaxation... Also Known as Dentists and Dance Chill Out Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek reminder to loosen your shoulders, unclench your jaw, and stop hunching over your phone. Perfect for ending a day of dentists and dancing with some stretching.
holidays.origin: This is a playful, unofficial observance in the spirit of wellness calendars, built around the idea of unwinding after a busy week. It has no single official founder and spreads mostly through wellness blogs and social posts.
holidays.funFact: Many people clench their jaws or grind their teeth without realizing it, especially when stressed, which is one reason dentists often check for signs of it.
